title: 2009 AMC 12B Problem 6
statement: By inserting parentheses, it is possible to give the expression \[2 \times 3 + 4 \times 5\] several values. How many different values can be obtained?

solutions.text:
The genuinely different groupings give

\((2 \times 3) + (4 \times 5) = 26,\) \(\ ((2 \times 3) + 4) \times 5 = 50,\) \(\ 2 \times (3 + (4 \times 5)) = 46,\) and \(\ 2 \times (3 + 4) \times 5 = 70.\)

These are all distinct, so \(4\) values can be obtained.

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: The result depends on when the addition is performed relative to the two multiplications
Enumerate the distinct groupings; several parenthesizations collapse to the same value
